notes: Alignment was by overlapping or adjacent anchors in the saved text. Almost all units matched (coders found nearly the same passages); coder A found extra units, mostly sub-items and restatements (checklist steps, definitions in template examples, the three talk topics) that B skipped as repeats; all were real policy statements and were kept. Disagreements were mostly (1) phase: before-course vs course-start vs general vs during-work for syllabus-element requirements and template statements, resolved by treating what the syllabus must tell students as course-start, and doing-the-work rules as during-work; (2) actor on rationale and example statements, resolved by who the sentence binds; (3) policy_type on boundary pairs (P09 vs P05 for the Prohibited/Permitted/Required elements, P28 vs P36 vs P24 for nondisclosure, P01 vs P19 for the blanket ban, P50 vs P59 for the data table), resolved by constant comparison with each type's wording and with the same sentence elsewhere; (4) unit_stance for rationale and example units, resolved as neutral unless the unit itself restricts or permits; (5) one document-level stance split (CSIT: A delegates, B permit), resolved as permit because the policy states its own default lists. UNCOVERED units were kept and annotated. No new types.
